question.text: Within how many days must shares be credited to the IEPF demat account after they become due for transfer to the IEPF?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says shares must be credited to the IEPF demat account within 30 days of such shares becoming due for transfer to the IEPF. That directly supports option D. The Trap: Option C (60 days) is the workbook timeline for filing Form IEPF-2 after the AGM, not for crediting shares to the IEPF demat account. Options A and B (7 and 15 days) do not match the workbook figure for this step and are easy to assume if a candidate conflates other corporate-action timelines. Note: The trigger for the 30-day clock is the shares becoming due for transfer to the IEPF; the workbook does not phrase the trigger as the date on which the transfer process is "initiated", which is a subtlety worth keeping straight when reading similarly worded questions.
